question: What is the main goal of community engagement in reproductive health?

options.A: Training foreign doctors to work in local clinics
options.B: Building more hospitals in rural communities
options.C: Reducing the cost of medical equipment importation
options.D: Involving local people directly in addressing health issues

explanation: Community engagement focuses on working side by side with local populations so they can actively shape health interventions that affect them. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h1)

question: Why are health programs more successful when the community helps design them?

options.A: It guarantees that government funding will double
options.B: Local people trust interventions they help create
options.C: It eliminates the need for any professional nurses
options.D: Foreign donors prefer funding community-built projects

explanation: When communities are involved from the start, programs align better with local realities, leading to higher trust and acceptance. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h1)

question: What is a major direct consequence of unsafe abortion resulting from an unintended pregnancy?
explanation: Unsafe abortions frequently lead to dangerous complications like severe bleeding and life-threatening infections. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h2)

question: A 16-year-old girl drops out of school due to an unplanned pregnancy. What long-term impact is she most likely to face?
explanation: Interrupting education early often limits future career opportunities, leading to long-term financial struggles. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h2)

question: Who are considered primary gatekeepers of cultural norms in many Nigerian communities?
explanation: Traditional and religious leaders hold significant influence over community values and must be engaged for health programs to succeed. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h3)

question: Why are adolescents and young adults categorized as a vulnerable population regarding unintended pregnancy?

options.A: They often lack autonomy and access to correct information
options.B: They are completely banned from entering any market areas
options.C: They always reject assistance from community health workers
options.D: They possess advanced medical degrees in pharmacology

explanation: Young people frequently face barriers in accessing reproductive health services and accurate guidance due to age-related stigma. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h3)

question: What is the primary advantage of mobile health clinics in reproductive health outreach?

options.A: Providing free cars to every pregnant woman
options.B: Replacing all permanent hospitals in urban centers
options.C: Eliminating the need for community health education
options.D: Bringing family planning supplies directly to remote villages

explanation: Mobile clinics bridge the geographical gap by bringing essential services closer to people who live far from standard health facilities. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h4)

question: Why might a teenager avoid visiting a local clinic for contraceptives even when the items are free?

options.A: The clinic only opens during midnight hours
options.B: Fear of being judged or seen by neighbors
options.C: Government rules forbid youth from walking outside
options.D: Contraceptives require a surgical procedure first

explanation: Stigma and lack of privacy in healthcare settings are major deterrents for young people seeking reproductive health services. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h4)

question: Which of the following is a common myth associated with modern contraceptives?

options.C: They eliminate the need for clean water
options.D: They cure all known infectious diseases

explanation: A widespread misconception is that using birth control will permanently stop a woman from getting pregnant in the future. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h5)

question: How should a nurse best respond to a community member expressing fear that birth control causes illness?

options.A: Ignore the comment because myths always disappear on their own
options.B: Listen patiently and provide accurate, empathetic education
options.C: Scold the person for spreading false neighborhood gossip
options.D: Refuse to treat the person until they change their mind

explanation: Empathetic communication and factual education build trust and help correct misinformation without making the client defensive. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h5)

question: What is a key role of a nurse acting as a community champion for reproductive health?

options.A: Writing national health insurance budget laws
options.B: Replacing traditional village chiefs in council meetings
options.D: Educating and advocating outside hospital walls

explanation: Community champions extend their reach into local spaces to educate populations and advocate for better health practices. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h6)

question: A midwife wants to gain the trust of a conservative community before introducing family planning education. What is the best initial step?

options.A: Distribute pamphlets written in a complex medical language
options.B: Listen actively to local concerns and respect cultural sensitivities
options.C: Demand that the village chief close down all local shrines
options.D: Threaten residents with withdrawal of all general healthcare

explanation: Building trust requires listening and showing respect for local culture before attempting to introduce sensitive health topics. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h6)

question: What does 'monitoring' primarily involve in community health programs?

options.A: Continuous tracking of service uptake and activities
options.B: Waiting until a five-year grant period finishes
options.C: Changing the geographic location of the clinic daily
options.D: Firing staff members who fail to meet quotas

explanation: Monitoring is an ongoing process of tracking day-to-day activities and service delivery metrics. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h7)

question: Why is fostering community ownership critical for the sustainability of a health intervention?

options.A: It guarantees that all medications will be manufactured locally
options.B: It means nurses no longer need to work in clinics
options.C: It ensures the program survives even after external funding ends
options.D: It allows the community to stop paying taxes permanently

explanation: When a community takes charge of a project, they maintain it independently long after outside financial support stops. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h7)
